Daily care standards for lighting levels

Purpose: this section keeps the Companion Animal Travel Desk steady, kind, and easy to trust while staff handle routine animal travel support.

Staff keep the desk calm, tidy, and well lit so travelers can read forms, check carriers, and settle in without strain. Soft, even light is best for animals and people alike, and glare on counters or screens should be reduced whenever possible. When a pet arrives, staff speak in a warm, simple way, confirm the booking details, and note any care concerns before the traveler moves on. Every animal receives patient attention from trained staff. If a passenger seems worried, the first response is to listen closely, stay relaxed, and give clear next steps without rushing.

Staff check that waiting areas stay clean, that water bowls and approved supplies are available, and that carriers are handled gently from one point to the next. Floors, seats, and counters should remain free of clutter so the space feels safe for pets and easy for travelers to use. If an animal appears uneasy, staff slow the pace, lower noise where they can, and ask for a senior coordinator when extra support is needed. Supervisors listen carefully when a passenger is worried. No staff member should guess about a pet's needs if the traveler has already shared useful details.

Travel desk records must be accurate, brief, and respectful. Write only what is needed for service, and keep personal comments out of the record. If a traveler offers instructions about feeding, handling, or comfort items, repeat them back in plain words so everyone understands. When an issue cannot be solved at the counter, staff should pass it along at once and keep the traveler informed while help is arranged. The tone should stay calm even during busy periods, because steady service helps both passengers and animals feel safe.

If anything seems uncertain, contact the senior coordinator or the duty supervisor right away.
